proposals.title: Affording to live near my work and family
proposals.line: I can pay the rent on a place close to my job and the people I love, so I'm not trading cheaper rent for an hour on the road each way.

screen.reason: Names the end state of affording rent close to work and family instead of trading cheaper rent for a long drive, which ties Commute's loss to this pain's cost.

overlaps.title: Staying in my home as long as I want
overlaps.reason: Both are about where I can afford to live, one about staying and one about being close to work and family.

proposals.title: Affording a place of my own
proposals.line: I can pay the rent on a place by myself, without needing roommates to cover it.

screen.reason: Names the end state of affording rent alone without roommates, which the roommate detail keeps distinct from Living with parents.

overlaps.title: Affording enough room for my family
overlaps.reason: Both are about what kind of place the rent lets me have, more space for a family or a place without roommates.

proposals.title: Knowing what my rent will be next year
proposals.line: When my lease comes up for renewal, I already know about what next year's rent will be, and I know I can pay it.

screen.reason: Names the end state of a future rent that is known in advance and affordable, tied to lease renewal rather than any other pain.

overlaps.title: Staying in my home as long as I want
overlaps.reason: Both protect against rent increases, one as a known number and one as not being pushed out.

proposals.title: Rent that leaves enough for everything else
proposals.line: After I pay rent each month, there's still enough for groceries, bills, and a little put away.

screen.reason: Names the end state of rent taking a share of pay small enough that groceries, bills, and some savings still fit, which is tied to rent and not to Broke or No savings.

overlaps.title: Paying a fair rent for the place I get
overlaps.reason: A fair rent may read as a way to rent that leaves enough for everything else.

proposals.title: Affording enough room for my family
proposals.line: We can afford a place where the kids have a bedroom and nobody sleeps on the couch, and we still cover our other bills.

screen.reason: Names the end state of a family affording a home with enough bedrooms while still covering other bills, which is the rent-for-space tradeoff of this pain.

overlaps.title: Affording a place of my own
overlaps.reason: Both are about what kind of place the rent lets me have, more space for a family or a place without roommates.

proposals.title: Paying a fair rent for the place I get
proposals.line: My rent matches what my place is really worth, and no hidden fees get added on top.

screen.reason: A rent that matches the place's worth with no added fees is wanted so I stop overpaying and keep more of my pay, which is the rent-leaves-room end inside this pain.

overlaps.title: Rent that leaves enough for everything else
overlaps.reason: A fair rent may read as a way to rent that leaves enough for everything else.

proposals.title: Housing payments that build something for me
proposals.line: Part of what I pay for housing each month adds up to savings or a share in my home, instead of just disappearing.

screen.reason: Housing payments that add up to savings or a share in my home fit Buying a home ("I can't afford to buy a home.") unchanged, and are about what payments build rather than paying too much.

proposals.title: Staying in my home as long as I want
proposals.line: I can keep living in the home and neighborhood I know for years, without a rent increase pushing me out.

screen.reason: Staying in my home for years without being pushed out fits Eviction ("I might lose my home.") and Gentrification just as well, since rent increases are a main way people lose their homes.

overlaps.reason: Both protect against rent increases, one as a known number and one as not being pushed out.

proposals.title: Rents in my town that ordinary paychecks can cover
proposals.line: Teachers, cooks, nurses, and people with jobs like mine can all afford to rent in my town.

screen.reason: Rents that teachers, cooks, and nurses can afford in my town fit Gentrification ("I see longtime neighbors priced out as my area gets more expensive.") unchanged.
